Night trains are back: the new routes for 2027

By Mara Lindqvist · 12 min read

Europe's sleeper network is growing again. Three new overnight routes join the timetable in December 2027, and older lines get modern carriages.

After a decade of cuts, overnight trains are returning to the timetable. Operators have ordered new sleeper carriages, and several cities that lost their night connections are being linked again.

The new routes

  • Brussels – Prague, three nights a week
  • Munich – Rome, every night from spring
  • Hamburg – Copenhagen – Stockholm, extended to Oslo in summer

All three leave in the evening and arrive before nine the next morning. Timetables were planned so that the trains pass busy junctions at night, when tracks are free.

What still holds the network back

Capacity remains small. A sleeper train carries a few hundred passengers, while a day train on the same line can carry more than a thousand.
